title: Boldog születésnapot!: Birthday and Name-Day Wishes

sections.title: Wishes for a birthday or name day
sections.content: You know *névnap* from Unit 37: in Hungary a name day is celebrated almost like a birthday (*születésnap*), because every day of the calendar belongs to some first names. You know the long wishes *Boldog névnapot kívánok!* and *Boldog születésnapot kívánok!* from Unit 37; the short forms are *Boldog születésnapot!* and *Boldog névnapot!* Both end in *-t*, the accusative you know from A1 (*kávét*, *könyvet*): the wish is short for *Kívánok neked boldog születésnapot* ("I wish you a happy birthday"; you know *kíván* from Unit 28). *Isten éltessen!* (you know it from Unit 37) is a fixed phrase for either day (literally "may God keep you alive"), and *Gratulálok!* means "Congratulations!" A birthday *torta* (A1) carries *gyertya* ("candles"), and a *csokor* ("bunch") of flowers is a typical gift.

sections.title: Key phrases
rows: Many happy returns! (birthday or name day)
I wish you a happy birthday!

items.english: I brought you a bunch of flowers.

sections.content: Do not drop the *-t*: say *Boldog születésnapot!*, not *Boldog születésnap!* The adjective *boldog* never changes; the ending belongs on the noun.
